messages.subject: Stacking order
parts:
I am not sure if this a bug of a feature, but I found an inconsistency in the stacking order, depending of the geometry being used. In the example below color/fill are based on a factor. geom_bar uses the levels of the factor to create the stacking order, while the rest do it alphabetically.

I run into this issue when I was trying to make a stacked area plot. I know I can fix the order manually, but I was wondering if the order should be consistent across geometries.

I am running R 1.15.1 and ggplot2 v0.9.2.1.

Thanks for your time,
Eduardo

___________________________

library(ggplot2)
data <- data.frame(
        g = rep(LETTERS[1:3], each=4),
        x = rep(1:4, 3),
        y = 1:12)
data$g <- factor(data$g, levels = c("B", "C", "A"))

# Bars ordered following the levels in the factor
ggplot(data, aes(x = x, weight = y, fill = g)) + geom_bar(binwidth = 0.5)

# Stacking order alphabetically
ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = g)) + geom_area()
ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y, color = g)) + geom_line(position = "stack")
ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y, color = g)) + geom_point(position = "stack")

# Stacking following the levels (like geom_bar)
ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = g, order = as.numeric(g))) + geom_area()
ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y, color = g, order = as.numeric(g))) + geom_line(position = "stack")
ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = y, color = g, order = as.numeric(g))) + geom_point(position = "stack")
